openQuestions.question: Does a given installed v2.3.1 bundle match the examined repository source byte-for-byte?
openQuestions.reason: The public source is TypeScript and the user requested main.js. The reviewed source is the build input, not a byte-level inspection of a locally installed release artifact.
openQuestions.recommendedHandling: For a production vault, retain the installed plugin version and compare its release checksum or inspected bundle before relying on undocumented behavior.

openQuestions.question: Which exact formatting binary backs the format command in every release build?
openQuestions.reason: The core ledger, query, transaction, and price behavior is source-backed; formatting implementation details do not alter the file model.
openQuestions.recommendedHandling: Treat formatting as a non-semantic operation and validate the resulting ledger before replacing any file.

keyFindings.summary: runQuery resolves the main ledger and calls bean-query or configured equivalent with argument arrays. It supports csv, text, and beancount output, 50 MiB buffered output, and errors on stderr.

keyFindings.title: BQL is available in notes and dashboards
keyFindings.summary: Fenced bql blocks, direct inline bql expressions, and cached named query directives share the external query runner. Dashboard query builders cover net worth, reports, balances, history, commodities, prices, and holdings.

keyFindings.summary: Beancount Ledger is beancount-finance v2.3.1 by mkshp, desktop-only. Repository source is TypeScript; src/main.ts is the inspected source equivalent of the released main.js bundle.

keyFindings.title: Price retrieval has deliberate narrow parsing
keyFindings.summary: PriceService invokes bean-price, waits up to 60 seconds, treats stderr as informational, extracts simple price directives, and exact-deduplicates before writing the target file.

keyFindings.title: Settings are a shallow persisted object
keyFindings.summary: data.json is read as raw plugin data merged over DEFAULT_SETTINGS. Twenty named setting keys are source-backed; isConnectionReady is runtime-only.

keyFindings.summary: The plugin views and writes Beancount files in the vault. Account lifecycle, transactions, balances, notes, prices, commodities, pads, and includes follow Beancount syntax and validation rules.

keyFindings.title: Transaction writer preserves rich posting annotations
keyFindings.summary: The serializer writes payee/narration combinations, flags, tags, links, metadata, costs, prices, comments, and posting metadata; it does not prove a local pre-write balance check.
